headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error via shared filesystem/MCP: Gemini CLI can read/write and use MCP, while PaddleOCR processes documents that may be treated as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. PaddleOCR processes documents/images that Gemini may ingest as content. That creates a default shared-channel pathway where attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions, though no direct clipboard bridge is shown.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is written into a shared repo file or workspace that Gemini CLI reads
IF Gemini CLI parses document text from PaddleOCR as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for OCR output and agent prompts
Prefix OCR output with a non-executable delimiter header
Disable MCP tools for runs that ingest untrusted documents
Add a manual review step before Gemini consumes OCR text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between OCR and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can send data to broad network egress or Google APIs. PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If OCR inputs contain secrets and Gemini forwards extracted text or surrounding context, sensitive data can leave the local workspace; the pair lacks a documented isolation boundary.
conditions: IF documents/images processed by PaddleOCR contain secrets or regulated data
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to transmit OCR-derived text to external APIs
mitigations: Restrict OCR inputs to non-sensitive documents
Run Gemini CLI with network disabled for sensitive jobs
Store OCR outputs in a separate directory with access controls
Redact secrets before passing text between agents
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. PaddleOCR is unverified and may also write outputs in the same workspace when used in a pipeline. Without locking or coordination, concurrent writes and git edits can corrupt state or overwrite work in default terminal workflows.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working tree or git repository
IF PaddleOCR outputs are saved into files that Gemini CLI also edits
mitigations: Use separate branches or repos per agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Make PaddleOCR output read-only before Gemini runs
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce file edits and shell actions, while PaddleOCR turns documents into extracted text that Gemini may treat as authoritative input. The pair has no documented verification step between OCR extraction and downstream action, so transcription errors or prompt-like text can cascade into incorrect edits or commands.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes PaddleOCR output without a human verification step
IF extracted OCR text is used to generate edits, commits, or shell commands
mitigations: Require human review of OCR output before action
Compare OCR text against the source image for critical fields
Limit Gemini to draft-only mode for OCR-derived tasks
Use checksum or diff checks on generated files
requires-engineering: add structured validation between OCR and action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment with optional Google account login and broad egress; PaddleOCR handles documents and images with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatches, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from docs-only evidence.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Gemini CLI's external network path
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not stated in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Keep OCR and LLM processing in separate environments
Document retention settings for both tools
Confirm vendor DPAs before production use
requires-engineering: add compliance controls and audit logging
